clue.text: Ah, not a smile from her, being framed

definitions.text: Ah, not a smile from her, being framed

indicators.note: framed in the sense of put together or constructed, so the letters of the opening words are built into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the woman in a picture frame is not smiling at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of AH NOT A SMILE rearrange into the answer, and the whole clue also describes the painting: a framed woman famous for an ambiguous half-smile.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait of a Florentine woman hangs framed in the Louvre and is famous for her faint, uncertain smile.

clue.text: Bird giving Leander's beloved direction

parts.note: in Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to visit his lover Hero
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A bird shows the way to the woman a legendary swimmer loved.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading water bird with a dagger bill.

clue.text: Overcomes the competition at Augusta

definitions.meaning: defeats or gets the better of
the US golf major played each April at Augusta National, Georgia

explanation.definitionFit: To beat something is to get on top of it; the Augusta golf tournament carries the same name.

clue.text: Fancy one going in-off

indicators.note: the numeral word is placed inside the other piece, entering it

parts.note: an event that is off is not on, cancelled
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A snooker or billiards player imagines potting the ball off another, an in-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in-off' looks like a snooker shot (potting a ball off another), but the hyphen splits it: 'going in' is the container signal and 'off' is a cancelled event.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is an idea or whim that comes into the mind.

clue.text: Perfume from the French salesman

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a vender (or vendor) is one who sells

explanation.surface: A scent is bought from a French seller.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant scent made from the oil of a purple-flowered plant.

clue.text: Muslem in a race between the Poles

indicators.note: the second piece is placed in the gap separating the two pole letters

parts.note: the two poles of the Earth are S and N, south and north
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Muslim athlete competes in a race against people from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Poles' suggests people from Poland, but it means the South and North poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval name for an Arab or Muslim, especially at the time of the Crusades.

clue.text: Radiate warmth as a lioness among her cubs

definitions.text: Radiate warmth as a lioness among her cubs

parts.words: Radiate warmth as a lioness among her cubs
parts.note: a proud mother shines with satisfaction, and a lioness lives in a group of lions called by the word for self-esteem

explanation.definitionFit: To beam with satisfaction at one's achievements or family, a lioness's family group being a pride.

clue.text: One with something to say at bridge

definitions.text: One with something to say at bridge

parts.words: One with something to say at bridge
parts.note: in the card game, the player who first named the trump suit plays the hand and is so called after announcing it

explanation.definitionFit: In contract bridge, the player who plays the hand for the side that won the auction, having first bid the final suit.

clue.text: Work with exercises in mind

parts.note: treatment of mental problems by talking and mental exercises, not physical training

explanation.definitionFit: Treatment of mental or emotional disorders by psychological means rather than medicine.

clue.text: Not publicans from the Upper House this select band of sportsmen

definitions.text: Not publicans from the Upper House this select band of sportsmen

parts.words: Not publicans from the Upper House this select band of sportsmen
parts.note: the group's name looks like innkeepers of the House of ..., but it is a cricketing charity club named after the London cricket ground

explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; the Lord's Taverners are a charity cricket club of celebrities, not peers who run pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A British charity whose celebrity members play cricket matches to raise money.

clue.text: See 10
Own winner and make a name for yourself!

annotationWithheld.why: Own winner and make a name for yourself! (3,6): OWN WINNER is an anagram of the answer but no clue word signals the anagram, so no honest parse is available as held
annotationWithheld.clue: Own winner and make a name for yourself!

clue.text: Suffering from depression, I note

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between two mountain peaks
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone says they are suffering from depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' looks like low mood, but it is a dip in a mountain ridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe abdominal pain, especially in babies, is a form of suffering.

clue.text: Be firm about one's position this month

indicators.note: the abbreviation for this month goes round the other piece, surrounding it

parts.note: inst. (instant) is the old business abbreviation for the current month
one's read as one is, giving I and IS

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to hold their ground over their stance this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is old letter-writing shorthand for this month; 'position' only completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand something firmly and not give way.

clue.text: Fancied a chiming clock?

definitions.meaning: a clock that has rung the hour has been hit upon by its hammer

explanation.definitionFit: To be smitten with someone is to be keen on them; a clock that has chimed has been hit by its striker.

clue.text: Forename associated with 1 across

parts.note: the first name of the Renaissance painter of the famous portrait at the first across entry

explanation.definitionFit: The given name of da Vinci, the Italian Renaissance artist who painted the famous smiling portrait.

clue.text: British composer on the river is Welsh

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits after the first, as if placed on it

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
Havergal Brian was an English composer of many symphonies

explanation.surface: A British composer living by a river is from Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambria is the Latin name for Wales, so the adjective means from Wales.

clue.text: Tough wood he-man Rob chopped

indicators.note: chopped up, so the letters of the strongman and his name are cut and reassembled

explanation.surface: A muscular man named Rob cut up some hard timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree of the birch family with very hard, tough timber.

clue.text: Seem likely to succeed with a reasonable offer

definitions.meaning: to promise well or look set to happen
an offer at auction that is just and decent

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for showing promise; read literally, an offer that is just.

clue.text: Burn up the track.

parts.note: to singe something, and also slang for driving very fast along a road

explanation.definitionFit: To singe the surface of something, and colloquially to drive at great speed.

clue.text: Vocal number the German Johnnie takes on

parts.note: a fielder who takes the ball has caught it, and C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
Hans is the German form of John or Johnny
taken as written

explanation.surface: A German man takes on a singing number.
explanation.walkthrough: C for caught is cricket shorthand: a catch is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A French song, especially a cabaret or music-hall song, is a sung number.

clue.text: Credit to Fife anyway, albeit in Perthshire

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: in any way, any old order, so the letters of the county name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A town does credit to Fife, though it actually lies in neighbouring Perthshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Fife and Perthshire are both Scottish counties; the town is in Perthshire, hence 'albeit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in central Scotland, in the county of Perthshire.

clue.text: … as a number in revolutionary garb did

indicators.note: the colour clothes the other pieces, wrapping round them as garb does

parts.note: red is the colour of revolutionaries and communists
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a runner dressed in red sped along.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 20 across: 'did' stands for 'burned up the track'.
explanation.definitionFit: Following on from the previous clue, did means drove or ran very fast.

clue.text: Critic in with a shout

parts.note: a heckler criticises by shouting, and in with a shout means having a chance

explanation.definitionFit: A heckler who jeers at sportsmen or speakers is a vocal critic.

clue.text: Toll for a monarch and his lady-love

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A tax levied on behalf of a king and his mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toll' looks like a charge but means the sound of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow ringing of a bell, as at a funeral, is its toll.

clue.text: Magazine's invitation to despairing anglers?

parts.note: a request to readers to write in, and literally a suggestion to put a fishing cord into the water

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for writing a short letter, which literally means lowering a fishing cord.

clue.text: Clean up in a lottery

definitions.meaning: a sweepstake, a draw for prize money

explanation.definitionFit: To brush dirt away with a broom; also short for a sweepstake draw.

clue.text: A flaring end staged in opera

definitions.text: A flaring end staged in opera

indicators.note: staged in the sense of arranged or put on, so the letters are presented in a new order

explanation.surface: An opera closes with a blazing climax on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The spectacular closing section of an opera or show.
